What matters when hiring for hospitals & clinics in Tamil Nadu

Chennai is one of India's largest healthcare markets, with dense hospital zones around Greams Road, Vadapalani, Porur and the OMR and GST Road corridors. Vellore draws patients from across India because of its large medical college hospital. Coimbatore, Madurai and Tiruchirappalli have their own big private hospitals. Experienced staff nurses trained in Tamil Nadu are in demand in many places, so they move often and hospitals plan for constant backfill.

Every nurse must hold current registration with the Tamil Nadu Nurses and Midwives Council. GNM and B.Sc Nursing holders are verified by registration number and renewal status. Lab technicians usually hold a DMLT or B.Sc MLT, and radiology staff need a recognised radiography qualification. Pharmacists must be registered with the Tamil Nadu Pharmacy Council. NABH-accredited hospitals also expect a credential file and documented competency checks for every clinical employee.

Hospitals run round the clock, and night duty is unavoidable for nursing and support staff. Women on night duty are covered by the consent and safety conditions in Section 43 of the OSH Code and the state's rules (as of Nov 2026). Housekeeping and attendant staff on contract need PF, and ESI where wages are within Rs 21,000 a month (ESIC, as of Nov 2026). Clinical establishments must also meet state registration rules.

What we check before sending candidates

  • Verify nursing council registration number and renewal status
  • Check Pharmacy Council registration for pharmacists
  • Confirm DMLT, B.Sc MLT or radiography qualification certificates
  • Ask clinical candidates which departments and bed sizes they have worked in
  • Check hepatitis B vaccination status where the hospital requires it
  • Confirm acceptance of night duty and rotational shifts

Answers

Hospitals & clinics hiring: questions employers ask

Do you verify nursing registration?

Yes. Every staff nurse profile we send includes the Tamil Nadu Nurses and Midwives Council registration number, and we check that the registration is current. Nurses registered in another state generally need Tamil Nadu registration to practise here. Your HR team or nursing superintendent should still see the original certificate on the joining day.

Can you send relief nurses for short leave cover?

Short-term nursing cover is possible for some roles, but it is harder than permanent hiring because many nurses want stable posts. Contract cover works well for ward aides, attendants and housekeeping. For nurses, give us the dates, ward type and shift pattern as early as you can. First profiles arrive within 48 hours for helpers and 7 days for skilled roles.

What is the replacement policy if a nurse leaves early?

Nurse turnover is high across Tamil Nadu, so replacement terms matter. Ours are set out in writing with every quote. As market context, recruitment agencies in India commonly give 30 to 90 days of free replacement for permanent hires. Ask any agency to put the replacement window, its conditions and its exclusions in writing before you sign an agreement.

Do NABH hospitals need anything extra from you?

NABH-accredited hospitals keep a credential file for each clinical employee, so we send copies of qualifications, council registration, experience letters and ID with every clinical profile. Competency assessment and privileging stay with the hospital's own clinical leads. Tell us your document checklist, and we collect it before the candidate is shortlisted.

How do fees work for hospital staffing?

Our hospital staffing fee is quoted in writing for each requirement before you commit. As a market reference, permanent hires through agencies are often priced at one to two months of salary, or 8.33% to 16.67% of annual CTC. Contract support staff are billed monthly with PF, ESI and a service charge, plus 18% GST, generally on the full invoice. These figures describe the market, not our rates.
